title: Clear on Size
concept: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission recommended stretching Mayor Grier Hopkins' proposed 12-month pause on permits for large data centers to 18 months. Per the News-Miner any one of three thresholds would trip it, at least 5 MW of power, 40,000 square feet or 5 MW made on site, and the planning director says 5 MW can power at least 3,000 homes, in a borough where the general use zone covers 97 percent of the land and anything goes. The line is clear on size before anyone knows where it reaches: the borough likely can't zone inside the Eielson Air Force Base fence, Hopkins believes a purely government-purpose data center would not be subject to the pause, private use might be different, and the borough is researching how to turn that gray area black and white. The fair test gives the reasons for time a full scene (diesel generators, anxiety over AI in general, a resident's call to take the time) and the opposite view the same weight (research due at month 10, the pause running 18, neither outlet says why). Nothing is law yet; the Assembly vote is likely January 14th. Drawn as Chalky, a faced safety-orange chalk-line reel snapping a dashed ultramarine line across the Tanana valley in a sunless mint afterglow, a cutaway of three PROPOSED trip pins tripped by dashed outlines, a map flooded sage, the chalk piling gray and going slack at the outside of the umber Eielson chain-link, three owned ropes lifting the slack line while an unheld coil carries the extra 8 months, a frosted stopwatch at zero with two sealed paint cans, and a reel-in to a bare frayed end beside two unstruck chalk marks.

divergence_note: The last films were open North Slope tundra in polar night and midnight-sun honey with a crowd of faced decision trees and radar lime (11-16), rain-black Juneau night at one door with a gunmetal letterbox under a sodium lamp and pencilled vellum (11-15), a rose-line dusk dome over a survey stake pulled by three parties and watched by a raven (11-12), and a pink-gold ice-fog noon in Fairbanks with a roof puck (11-11). This film is a clear mint-afterglow afternoon with no sun over lilac snow and sage, its hero ONE small safety-orange surveyor's tool that moves through the valley drawing a line, its signal colour ultramarine chalk, its fence rust-brown, and fog only at the fence. Honest overlaps: 11-12 also had people pulling on something, answered by ropes that LIFT a slack line with the hero pulling with them, owned reasons, and no stake, tag or raven; 11-11 was also Fairbanks, answered by a sunless afterglow instead of a pink-gold sun in fog; 11-15 drew proposals dashed, answered by snapped chalk with powder and string texture and never pencil on vellum; 10-29 ended on blank shipping tags, answered here by a bare frayed line end and unstruck chalk marks; 10-23's rule stopped at a fence, answered by chalk that piles at the outside of the wire and goes slack. The hero's safety orange is pushed away from 11-16's thermometer red.

treatment.title: Clear on Size
treatment.summary: Dramatist winner with grafts, restaged at Gate 0. CHALKY, a dented safety-orange surveyor's chalk-line reel in an olive knit earflap hat, snaps a dashed ultramarine chalk line across the Tanana valley snow in the clear mint afterglow of a Fairbanks winter afternoon; its far end runs into a bank of ice fog (loop 1). A faceless figure tagged MAYOR GRIER HOPKINS pinches a chalk mark at 12 on the line, and the commission row pulls six more feet off the spool and marks 18 inside a dashed RECOMMENDED border. A cutaway inside the reel shows three trip pins under PROPOSED THRESHOLDS, each tripped by a dashed hypothetical block outline, a dashed RECOMMENDED flag popping, the line never clamping a building. One GVEA wire carries a spring-green pulse into a dashed 5 MW outline and the valley's windows light to AT LEAST 3,000 HOMES while Earl, a faceless plugged-in pickup, shivers in the lot (only here and at the button). The map floods sage across 97 of 100 squares; a parka figure tagged ANY BUILDER reads the line and wonders when it turns to paint (loop 2). Chalky walks the line under the wire into fog; hard cut to the Eielson chain-link (rust-brown wire, nothing behind it but snow and spruce): the chalk stops at the OUTSIDE of the wire, piles gray there and the line goes slack. Hedged cards hang on the wire; a gray swatch with blank black and white halves. Act 3, THE FAIR TEST: three named reasons for time each tie a rope that LIFTS the slack line, Chalky pulling with them (a commissioner with a diesel genset icon on the rope tag, another commissioner hearing anxiety over AI in general, a resident), then the opposite view gets the same physical language, the line past month 10 lying on the snow as a long unheld slack coil, THE EXTRA 8 MONTHS, NEITHER OUTLET SAYS WHY, and the builder picks up its end. At the borough building a frosted stopwatch hangs at zero by NOT LAW YET with two sealed paint cans at its foot; a dashed ghost hand previews the sweep the vote would start. Chalky reels in through the fog: the end comes out bare and frayed, and two dashed chalk marks wait on the snow to be struck, RULES A BUILDER CAN MEET and AN ANSWER AT THE FENCE. The camera cranes up for the signature: the line crisp across the valley, slack and gray at the outside of the far chain-link, Earl still shivering, and Chalky re-snaps it.
treatment.judge_reasoning: P2 has the only real dramatic turn: the line is strained by legitimate concerns and the hero answers by reeling IN to find where it ends, which is the angle, readiness not refusal. It ends on a bare frayed line end beside two unstruck chalk marks and sealed paint cans, so it never claims the answer, and the chalk reel is fresh against the shelf (P1 and P4 repeat 11-15's pencil vellum and ink pen). Grafts fix its weak explanation (P3's moving OR cutaway) and add the even-handed upside (P4's builder reads the line) and a wordless runner (P1's Earl).

angle.thesis: Fairbanks has drawn a clear line on size before it knows where that line reaches, so the 18 months become readiness, not refusal, only if they end with rules a builder can meet and an answer on the government-purpose gray area at the Eielson fence.
supporting_facts: The line is precise. Any one of at least 5 MW drawn, 40,000 square feet or 5 MW made on site, and 5 MW is enough for at least 3,000 homes per the planning director (c6, c7, c8, c9, c10).
The rules vacuum is real. General Use One covers 97 percent of the borough and anything goes in general use, so today a builder has no standard to meet either way (c11, c12).

The reach is not settled. The borough likely can't zone inside the Eielson fence, Hopkins believes a purely government-purpose data center would not be subject to the pause, private use might be different, and the borough is researching how to turn that gray area black and white (c15, c16, c17, c18).
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: The people asking for time have real reasons and get a scene at full strength. A commissioner warned most of these data centers come with diesel generators, another is hearing anxiety over AI in general, Hopkins points to the sheer scale other cities are seeing, and a resident called it smart to take the time (c19, c20, c22, c23). The opposite fair case also stands, research is due at month 10 while the pause runs 18, neither outlet reports why, and a governor-elect would support a statewide pause (c3, c5, c26, c27). The film never hints at a motive and never says a project is coming.
angle.falsifier: The borough's research already shows a purely government-purpose data center falls under the pause, so the size line and its reach are the same line, or the 10-month report ends with no standards a builder could meet and only another extension.
angle.not_an_ai_vote: The thresholds are size and power. AI appears only as the News-Miner's national framing and one commissioner's quote (c20, c21). Say early, on screen, that it isn't a vote on AI.

runners_up.angle: A pause with a size line is how Fairbanks gets ready to say yes (Alaska-win)
runners_up.why_lost: too generous to call the line clear on reach, and speaks for a borough whose Assembly hasn't voted; its exit test (rules a builder can meet) is grafted in

runners_up.angle: Residents want time to answer grid, diesel and siting, not a verdict on AI (local concern)
runners_up.why_lost: one resident on record, the diesel worry is a commissioner's, and it implies a project is coming; it becomes the Act 3 fair-test scene

runners_up.angle: The line only reaches private projects on borough land (structural, v1)
runners_up.why_lost: turned Hopkins's belief into a ruling and read the grid as excluded when the borough plans to ask

angle.who_it_serves: Assembly members heading into the public hearing and the likely January 14th vote, Golden Valley Electric members whose grid answer isn't in yet, residents whose concerns are on the record, and builders who need a clear line more than a long one (c13, c25, c28).

open_loop.what: Where does the line end? Planted when the snapped line's far end runs off into a bank of ice fog under WHERE DOES IT END?, kept as the fog swallowing the line on the walk and the line going slack at the outside of the Eielson wire, paid when Chalky reels the line in and its end slides out of the fog bare and frayed while two dashed chalk marks wait on the snow to be struck, RULES A BUILDER CAN MEET and AN ANSWER AT THE FENCE.

open_loop_2.what: When does it turn to paint? Planted as a bubble over the parka builder holding a chalk stick and a paint can with a question mark over the can, kept as two sealed paint cans at the foot of a frosted stopwatch at zero under NOT LAW YET, paid when the vote sign ASSEMBLY VOTE · LIKELY JAN 14TH drops and the sealed can lids rattle, so the cans visibly key to the vote.
